subject: mathematics
question_text: Find λ if the points A(3, 2, 1), B(4, λ, 5), C(4, 2, −2) and D(6, 5, −1) are coplanar.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.70, chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Short Answer question 14. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The split gives half the marks to the determinant and a full mark to the substitution check, because a coplanarity value is only proved once it is put back. APPEARANCE: the book prints the tag "(Mar-2016(TS))" inline with this stem — the only printed exam year in this chapter — and appearances[] records year 2016 with no board key, which this schema already reads as ts_ipe. That year is the SOURCE BOOK'S claim; it has NOT been checked against a TSBIE question paper, so it stays under needs_teacher_verification with the mark split. Both evaluations of the determinant agree at 35 − 7λ: the first-row expansion gives 9 − 7(λ − 2) + 12, and the second-row expansion gives 2λ + 8 + 27 − 9λ; computing AC × AD = (9, −7, 3) and dotting with AB gives 35 − 7λ a third time. Substituting λ = 5 gives 9 − 21 + 12 = 0 exactly. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, each worth 4 marks, under the 2026-27 pattern; Product of Vectors supplies one of them. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find λ — the vectors you form, the condition you use, and how you check the value.

steps.label: Form the edge vectors
steps.margin_note: First mark. Any of the four points may be the corner; A is the tidiest because λ then sits in one row only.
steps.memory_tip: Subtract the corner's coordinates from the other three points, one row each.

recall.must_convey: That the three edges from A are formed and their box product set to zero.
accept: take A as the corner and write AB, AC and AD
four points coplanar means the box product of the three edges is zero
subtract A from B, C and D
A ni corner ga teeskuni moodu edges rasi box product zero pettali
form AB AC AD and set their triple product to zero

steps.why: Four points lie in one plane exactly when three edges drawn from one of them are coplanar, and coplanar vectors have box product zero.
common_mistakes: Subtracting in the wrong order, for example A − B.
Using the four position vectors instead of the three edges.

steps.label: Set the determinant to zero
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. λ sits in the first row only, so the expansion is a straight line in λ.
steps.memory_tip: Expand along the row that carries λ once; the result is linear in λ.

accept: expand the determinant and get thirty five minus seven lambda
the middle term is minus seven into lambda minus two
row two gives the same thirty five minus seven lambda
determinant expand cheste thirty five minus seven lambda vasthundi
the expansion is linear in lambda

steps.why: Expanding the same determinant along a second row must give the same expression in λ; that is the cheapest guard against a sign slip.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the minus in front of the middle entry of the first row.

steps.label: Solve for λ and check
steps.margin_note: Last mark. One line of substitution proves the value; do not leave it out.
steps.memory_tip: Put the value back in. Coplanar means the determinant is exactly 0, not nearly 0.

recall.must_convey: That 35 − 7λ = 0 gives λ = 5, and that substituting it makes the determinant zero.
accept: set thirty five minus seven lambda to zero so lambda is five
put five back and the determinant is exactly zero
lambda five vasthundi, substitute chesi zero ani check cheyyali
solve the linear equation and check the value

steps.why: Putting the value back into the determinant is what turns a candidate into an answer; here it comes out exactly zero.
common_mistakes: Stopping at 35 − 7λ without setting it to zero.
